title: Battle of Gettysburg
summary: The bloodiest battle of the American Civil War ended Robert E. Lee's second invasion of the North and is generally regarded as the war's turning point.
description: Seeking a victory north of the Mason–Dixon line that might force a negotiated end to the war, Confederate general Robert E. Lee led his army into Pennsylvania. The armies met at Gettysburg, about 35 miles (56 km) south-west of Harrisburg, and fought for three days.

On the final day, Confederate troops attacked the Union centre on Cemetery Ridge in what became known as Pickett's Charge; the few who reached their objective were repulsed. The battle was a crushing Confederate defeat.
context: With more than 50,000 estimated casualties, Gettysburg was the bloodiest single battle of the conflict. Its defeat dashed Confederate hopes of becoming an independent nation.

facts.text: The battle was fought from 1 to 3 July 1863.
It ended in a Union victory and a Confederate retreat.

uncertain.text: Casualty totals are estimates; the American Battlefield Trust gives 'more than 50,000'.
